prompt: Design our annual SOX ITGC calendar. We're a calendar-year accelerated filer and remediation always surprises us in Q4.
assertions: Lays out a quarterly rhythm: Q1 scoping refresh/RCM updates, Q2 walkthroughs + interim testing, Q3 second testing wave + deficiency triage while remediation windows remain, Q4 roll-forward/update testing, remediation validation, aggregation analysis, management's 404(a) conclusion
Places user access reviews quarterly and terminations/privileged-access checks as continuous — the classic late-surprise sources
Builds remediation timing logic: controls fixed late can't demonstrate sufficient operating history — deficiencies found in Q3 or earlier leave a re-test window; that's why triage belongs mid-year
Includes deficiency aggregation and severity classification (AS 2201/Reg S-X ladder) ahead of the year-end conclusion, with audit-committee reporting for significant deficiencies

References current context accurately where used: COSO 2013 as the framework, PCAOB inspection focus on ICFR, ~8% of recent annual reports disclosing material weaknesses with IT/access among top themes
